title: JMAP: jmap-chat-push: content pushes a phone can render
description:
In scope by decision mimid-1wgh.98 (Mark, 2026-11-22). Not planned: read the draft, face the tension below, and put a plan in this field for Mark before any code.

WHAT THE DRAFT DOES. Reverses mimid-1wgh.12.30 (no PushSubscription) for this draft. chatPush delivers a ChatMessagePush with message metadata and an optional body snippet so a phone renders a notification with no follow-up request.

THE TENSION, to settle first: mimid's provider holds ciphertext and cannot produce a body snippet. The agent holds plaintext and already does exactly this for IRC over soju.im/webpush (crates/mimid-agent-irc/src/webpush.rs, RFC 8291 encryption to the client's keys, RFC 8292 VAPID). So the likely shape is the AGENT serving chatPush to its local clients, with the provider serving metadata-only pushes at most. Read the draft against what an E2EE deployment can honestly send, and report to Mark whether the draft needs a paragraph saying so.
design:
PLAN for Mark, written 2026-11-22 after reading
draft-atwood-jmap-chat-push-00 (357 lines) and the existing push code.

1. THE TENSION IS ALREADY SETTLED BY THE DRAFT. No decision needed.

§e2ee is explicit: the server derives `encrypted` from `bodyType` --
false for text/plain, text/markdown and application/jmap-chat-rich, true
otherwise unless it knows the type is plaintext. When true, `bodySnippet`
is absent, and `hasMention` and `mentionScopes` are absent too, because
mentions live inside the ciphertext. The remaining fields (messageId,
chatId, chatKind, chatName, senderId, senderDisplayName, sentAt,
encrypted) are stated to carry enough for "New message from Alice".

So a provider holding only ciphertext is a case the draft designed for,
not a conflict. (This also matches the correction made earlier today:
the claim that the draft conflicts with E2EE was false.)

2. WHERE IT GOES: BOTH ENDPOINTS, EACH DOING WHAT IT CAN.

- The AGENT's endpoint (mimid-agent-jmap) gets the full thing:
  bodySnippet, hasMention, mentionScopes, mute suppression and mention
  urgency, because the agent holds plaintext. This is the one with user
  value: it is what wakes a phone with something readable.
- The PROVIDER's endpoint (mimid-server/src/jmap) gets the metadata-only
  shape, `encrypted` true and no snippet. Honest and cheap, and it is
  all a provider can ever offer. Lower priority; propose doing it second
  or deferring it, since a stock client pointed at the provider cannot
  read the body anyway.

3. PREREQUISITE, and the reason this is cheaper than it looks.

The machinery already exists and was built front-end-agnostic:
- mimid_agent_store::push keeps subscriptions keyed BY FRONT END --
  register(&Subscription), unregister(front_end, endpoint),
  list(front_end) -- and holds the VAPID key in the agent's database.
  Nothing about the schema needs to change; JMAP registers with
  front_end = "jmap" beside IRC's.
- RFC 8291 encryption and RFC 8292 VAPID are implemented in
  crates/mimid-agent-irc/src/push_crypto.rs (310 lines) with ZERO
  references to IRC, on RustCrypto crates already in the build.

So step one is to MOVE push_crypto from mimid-agent-irc to
mimid-agent-store, beside the push module that already owns the
subscriptions and the key. No behaviour change for IRC, and it stops
mimid-agent-jmap needing to depend on the IRC crate, which the crate map
would not allow. This is a refactor with its own tests passing
unchanged, and should land as a separate commit before any JMAP code.

4. THEN, on the agent's endpoint:
- RFC 8620 PushSubscription/get and /set. NOTE this reverses decision
  mimid-1wgh.12.30 (no PushSubscription) for this draft, which the
  parent decision mimid-1wgh.98 already allows.
- The ChatPushConfig extension on PushSubscription (§chat-push-config):
  per-Chat filtering, urgency, mentionUrgency.
- Building ChatMessagePush from the store's records on a new inbound
  message, and the §delivery SHOULD NOTs: nothing for a message stored
  before the subscription, nothing for the account owner's own messages,
  nothing once the account has left the Chat, nothing for a muted Chat
  unless a broadcast mention resolves to the owner, nothing from a
  blocked ChatContact. Note the explicit clarification that a plain
  @user mention does NOT bypass mute; only a broadcast mention does.
- Urgency: if any entry in a batch has a mention, the WHOLE payload is
  sent at mentionUrgency, per §urgency.

5. ONE THING TO DECIDE WHILE IMPLEMENTING, not now: the draft puts
"SHOULD NOT set chatPush on a non-Web-Push endpoint" on the CLIENT.
mimid could instead refuse such a subscription, or accept it and fall
back to RFC 8620 StateChange as §e2ee describes. Recommend accepting and
falling back, because refusing would leave a phone with no wake-up at
all, and record it as a decision bead either way.

6. TESTS, following the fixture rule where it applies: the draft's
§"Example Payload" is an outside fixture and should be decoded, compared,
re-encoded and required byte-identical. Plus the delivery matrix
(own message, left chat, muted, muted with broadcast mention, blocked
contact) and the encrypted case asserting bodySnippet, hasMention and
mentionScopes are absent rather than empty.

NOT STARTED. The bead says a plan goes here before any code, so this is
the plan. Step 3 (the push_crypto move) is safe and useful on its own if
Mark wants progress before approving the rest.
notes:
CORRECTION, 2026-11-22: this bead's description says mimid's provider cannot produce a snippet and asks whether the draft needs a paragraph saying what an E2EE deployment omits. The first half is true; the second is wrong. jmap-chat-push already has an 'encrypted' flag (true when the server cannot produce a plaintext snippet), makes bodySnippet, hasMention and mentionScopes MUST-absent in that case, and carries a §e2ee section and a design principle covering exactly this. No draft change is needed. The error came from reading only the introduction.

SETTLED by decision mimid-1wgh.103: the provider serves chatPush in metadata-only mode (encrypted=true), configurable, default ON. The documentation beside the switch must say that with it on, the push operator learns who messaged whom and when.

STILL TO PLAN: which ChatMessageEntry properties the provider actually serves (it must support the listed minimum, but mentions and snippets are absent when encrypted), maxSnippetBytes and maxMessagesPerPush advertisement, per-chat and per-kind filtering, urgency values, and the mute and block interactions in the delivery section. Whether a user's own always-on agent also sends richer plaintext pushes, as the IRC front end does, is a separate question and not part of this bead.
